Could you find out the average percentage of the total lifetime sales (LTV) that occur in the first 7 and 30 days after a customer's initial purchase? The 7- and 30-day periods should be based on the exact number of hours-minutes-seconds, not calendar days.

WITH customer_first_payments AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id,
    MIN(payment_date) as first_payment_date
  FROM payment
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_ltv AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id,
    SUM(amount) as total_ltv
  FROM payment
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT 
  ROUND(AVG(sales_7days / total_ltv * 100.0), 4) as avg_pct_7days,
  ROUND(AVG(sales_30days / total_ltv * 100.0), 4) as avg_pct_30days,
  ROUND(AVG(total_ltv), 4) as avg_total_ltv
FROM (
  SELECT 
    p.customer_id,
    cl.total_ltv,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (p.payment_date - cf.first_payment_date)) / 3600.0 <= 168.0 THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) as sales_7days,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (p.payment_date - cf.first_payment_date)) / 3600.0 <= 720.0 THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) as sales_30days
  FROM payment p
  JOIN customer_first_payments cf ON p.customer_id = cf.customer_id
  JOIN customer_ltv cl ON p.customer_id = cl.customer_id
  WHERE cl.total_ltv > 0
  GROUP BY p.customer_id, cl.total_ltv
) sub

customer_totals AS (

)
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(100.0 * sales_7_days / ltv), 2) as avg_pct_7_days,
    ROUND(AVG(100.0 * sales_30_days / ltv), 2) as avg_pct_30_days,
